tools.name: set_effort
tools.description:
set_effort: set your reasoning effort for the requests after this call. A level you set holds across turns, over the automatic rules, until you call set_effort with auto.
auto hands the effort back to the automatic rules: each turn starts at its planned level, and failing test runs raise it.
Main chat only: a sub-agent never calls it.
Call it in your first response of a user turn whose work needs another level than the one in effect, alongside your first tool calls.
- xhigh: a decision others will build on (architecture, design trade-offs, a spec, a review verdict), or a root cause one attempt did not find; and anything heavier, which this setup caps at xhigh.
- high: debugging a known symptom, writing non-trivial code from scratch, explaining unfamiliar code.
- medium: edits whose every line the plan already fixes (a rename, a move, a known fix), running and reading tests; and anything lighter (lookups, status reports, formatting, one-line edits).
Raise it the moment the work turns harder than planned: a test fails for a reason you cannot name, or a fix you were sure of did not hold. Lower it once only mechanical steps remain.
If the answer itself needs deep thought and there is no tool work, call this first and answer after its result.

tools.name: effort_up
tools.description: Raise your own reasoning effort one step for your next replies. Use it when you are stuck: a check still fails after your fix, results do not fit your understanding of the code, a sub-task came back red for a reason you did not foresee — or right before a design decision that is hard to undo. Not for routine steps; it makes every later reply slower and costlier. The level then holds, whatever happens, until you call effort_auto.

tools.name: effort_down
tools.description: Lower your own reasoning effort one step for your next replies. Use it when what is left is routine: spawning and waiting, relaying results, bookkeeping, or a fix whose every line you already know. The level then holds, whatever happens, until you call effort_auto.

tools.name: effort_auto
tools.description: Hand your reasoning effort back to the automatic rules: it returns to your home level, and failing checks or red sub-tasks raise it again. Use it once the reason you called effort_up or effort_down is behind you.
